What happens when ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini all go down at the exact same time?

We just witnessed a highly unusual event in the AI infrastructure space. Yesterday, multiple leading foundation models experienced simultaneous service interruptions, exposing our growing dependency on these systems.

Here are the key developments from the last 24 hours that you should have on your radar:

🚨 A rare overlapping downtime hit ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini practically simultaneously. Around 11 AM ET on Thursday, users faced error messages, with OpenAI reporting elevated errors across both ChatGPT and Codex before services were restored.

📈 OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra demonstrated strong analytical capabilities in a new financial-review workflow. Using the model, Legora reviewed 41 documents in minutes, successfully identifying all four planted errors and boosting overall performance by nearly 40%.

💻 Replit Agent is showing how far non-technical builders can go without writing manual code. In a recent test of its free mode, the tool connected to Slack and Google Calendar to turn a rough concept into a working app, brand assets, and a live website.

🌤️ Google DeepMind officially announced WeatherNext 3, which the company is calling its most advanced and accurate global weather AI model to date.

As developers, we often build under the assumption that these APIs will always be available. Events like yesterday's multi-platform outage are a strong reminder to design robust fallback systems in our production applications.

If you rely on these models for your daily development workflow, how did yesterday's multi-model outage affect your productivity?
